title: Tight fast-correlation security boundary for SNOW 5G
summary: Determine the exact maximum absolute correlation of the relevant linear approximations of the original SNOW 5G stream cipher and the resulting tight fast-correlation attack bound.

formal_statement.body: For the original SNOW 5G specification, including the two $16$-bit modular additions in its finite-state machine, let $\rho_{\max}$ be the maximum absolute correlation over all linear approximations admitted by the source's fast-correlation framework. Determine $\rho_{\max}$ exactly and derive the corresponding tight time, data, and memory complexity boundary for fast correlation attacks.

scope.domain: Linear cryptanalysis and fast correlation attacks on SNOW 5G
assumptions: The original SNOW 5G specification is used, rather than its XOR-only variant
The finite-state machine retains its two additions modulo $2^{16}$
The attack and linear-approximation model is the one used by the source
parameters: time, data, and memory trade-off parameters
scope.unresolved_remainder: A known approximation gives $\rho_{\max}\ge 2^{-67.67}$, while later published work gives the untight theoretical bound $\rho_{\max}\le 2^{-62}$ and a balanced-attack lower bound of about $2^{260}$. The exact maximum correlation and the resulting tight attack-complexity boundary remain unknown.

citations.label: Ma et al., SNOW-family fast-correlation security question
Liu--Yang--Tian, SNOW 5G linear approximation
citations.locator: IACR Transactions on Symmetric Cryptology 2024(2), pp. 141--165

progress.summary: A concrete linear approximation with absolute correlation $2^{-67.67}$ supplies the current lower bound on the maximum correlation.
The source states that the theoretical fast-correlation resistance boundary of the original SNOW 5G has not been determined.
citation_labels: Ma et al., SNOW-family fast-correlation security question

progress.summary: Later published work derives an untight upper bound $2^{-62}$ for the maximum correlation of the $16$-bit-adder variant identified with SNOW 5G, implying a balanced-attack lower bound near $2^{260}$ without determining the exact boundary.
